title: Life of Adam and Eve — Hobah Translation
about: The Greek Adam-and-Eve apocalypse commonly called the Apocalypse of Moses. It recounts the fall, the penitence of Adam and Eve, Adam's final illness and death, and Eve's death. This is distinct from the much later First Book of Adam and Eve already in the library.

translation.base_text: Greek recension in C. von Tischendorf, Apocalypses Apocryphae (1866), as preserved in the public-domain Greek textual tradition and compared with the Online Critical Pseudepigrapha transcription
translation.method: Fresh modern-English rendering from the Greek recension; wording is independent of modern copyrighted English translations. Chapter divisions follow the Greek tradition. Obvious textual damage or uncertainty is left bracketed rather than silently repaired.
translation.confidence: Medium-high for the narrative sense; medium for places where Tischendorf's nineteenth-century Greek text is text-critically uncertain
translation.notes: Tischendorf's Greek recension is useful but not the final critical text. The Hobah edition therefore treats its wording as a manuscript-recension translation, not a reconstruction of the lost archetype.
translation.license_note: Ancient text and 1866 Greek edition are public domain. Hobah English wording is newly prepared for this project.

chapters.label: Chapter 1
chapters.text: After Adam and Eve had gone out of Paradise, they made themselves a shelter and mourned for seven days in great grief. When the seven days were finished they became hungry and looked for food, but they found nothing like the food they had known in the garden. Only food fit for animals was before them. Adam said to Eve, ‘Rise. Let us search, so that we may find something by which we can live and not perish.’

chapters.label: Chapter 2
chapters.text: They walked through the land and found no food such as they had eaten in Paradise, but only herbs and seed for beasts. Eve said, ‘God appointed these things for the animals. What shall we eat?’ Adam answered, ‘Let us repent with great repentance. Perhaps God will have mercy on us and give us something for life.’

chapters.label: Chapter 3
chapters.text: Eve asked, ‘What kind of repentance shall I do? Do not lay on me more than I can bear, lest I fail again.’ Adam said, ‘You cannot endure as much as I can. I will remain forty days in the Jordan, and you remain thirty-seven days in the Tigris. Stand in the water with a stone beneath your feet and let no word come from your mouth, for we are unworthy to pray openly. Let your whole heart be turned toward God.’

chapters.label: Chapter 4
chapters.text: Eve went to the Tigris and Adam to the Jordan. Adam entered the river until the water reached his neck. He said to the river, ‘Mourn with me, all created things around me, for I have sinned against the God who made you.’ The waters and creatures joined the sorrow, and Adam stood in repentance.

chapters.label: Chapter 5
chapters.text: Eve likewise stood in the Tigris. But Satan heard of their repentance and was distressed, because their turning back to God opposed his purpose. He took the appearance of a radiant angel and went weeping to Eve.

chapters.label: Chapter 6
chapters.text: He said, ‘Come out of the water. God has heard your repentance and ours. He has sent me to bring you food, as in the beginning.’ Eve believed the appearance and came out. When she reached the bank, she saw that his feet were unlike those of an angel and understood that she had been deceived again.

chapters.label: Chapter 7
chapters.text: Eve fell on the ground and cried, ‘Woe to me! Why do you pursue me? What have I done to you that you deceive me again?’ The adversary answered, ‘All my hostility toward you is because of Adam. Through him I was cast down from my glory.’

chapters.label: Chapter 8
chapters.text: Eve asked him how this happened. He said that when Adam was made in the image of God, Michael called the angels to honour the image God had formed. Michael bowed first and commanded the others to do likewise, but the adversary refused, saying that he was older than Adam and would not bow to one made after him.

chapters.label: Chapter 9
chapters.text: Other angels under his authority also refused. Michael warned them that rebellion would provoke God's anger, but the adversary said that if God became angry he would set his throne above the stars and make himself like the Most High. Then God cast him and his companions from their glory to the earth. ‘Because of you,’ he told Eve, ‘I lost my place; therefore I sought your ruin.’

chapters.label: Chapter 10
chapters.text: When Eve heard this she cried out and returned toward Adam. Adam saw her before the appointed time and said, ‘What has happened? How were you deceived again?’ Eve could not answer for grief. Adam lamented that their enemy had not ceased attacking them.

chapters.label: Chapter 11
chapters.text: Adam called to God: ‘O Lord, command this enemy to depart from us. Do not let him destroy the work of your hands.’ At Adam's prayer the adversary withdrew. Adam continued his forty days of repentance in the Jordan.

chapters.label: Chapter 12
chapters.text: When the days were completed, Adam came out of the river. He and Eve began again to seek food. Eve was pregnant, and when the time of birth came she was in great pain. She cried to Adam, ‘I am dying. Go and pray for me.’

chapters.label: Chapter 13
chapters.text: Adam prayed: ‘Lord, have mercy on her, for this pain has come because of our transgression.’ Twelve angels and two heavenly powers came to Eve, and Michael stood at her right side. Eve gave birth to a son, and the pain ceased. They named the child Cain.

chapters.label: Chapter 14
chapters.text: Afterward Eve bore Abel. She had dreamed that Cain drank his brother's blood and that it would not remain in his mouth. Adam and Eve were troubled by the dream and tried to keep the brothers apart, making Cain a farmer and Abel a shepherd.

chapters.label: Chapter 15
chapters.text: Yet Cain rose against Abel and killed him. When Adam was one hundred and thirty years old, Eve bore another son in place of Abel, and they called him Seth. Adam said, ‘God has given us another seed instead of Abel whom Cain killed.’

chapters.label: Chapter 16
chapters.text: After Seth, Adam and Eve had other sons and daughters. Adam lived many years and taught his children. When the end of his life approached, illness entered his body and he cried aloud in pain.

chapters.label: Chapter 17
chapters.text: Eve and all his children gathered around him. They asked, ‘Father, what is sickness and pain? Why do you suffer?’ Adam answered, ‘My children, this has come upon me because of sin.’ They asked him to tell them how the transgression happened.

chapters.label: Chapter 18
chapters.text: Adam said, ‘God placed me and your mother in Paradise and gave us every tree for food except one. He warned us that on the day we ate from it we would die. Your mother was separated from me while the angels who guarded us went up to worship God. The enemy found her alone.’

chapters.label: Chapter 19
chapters.text: Eve then took up the account. ‘The serpent came to me, but the adversary spoke through it. He asked why we did not eat from every tree. I told him God's command. He answered that God knew our eyes would be opened and that we would become like gods. He swore that the fruit was good and led me to the tree.’

chapters.label: Chapter 20
chapters.text: ‘When I came to the tree I saw the glory that had covered it. The adversary made me swear that I would also give the fruit to Adam. Then he climbed into the tree and put the poison of his wickedness upon the fruit, the root of desire and greed. I took it and ate.’

chapters.label: Chapter 21
chapters.text: ‘At once I knew that I had been stripped of the righteousness that had clothed me. I saw my nakedness and wept. The trees before which I passed dropped their leaves, except the fig tree. From its leaves I made a covering, because from it I had eaten.’

chapters.label: Chapter 22
chapters.text: ‘I called Adam and said, “Come, and I will show you a great mystery.” When he came I gave him the fruit. He ate, and his eyes were opened. He cried against me, “What have you done? You have separated me from the glory of God.”’

chapters.label: Chapter 23
chapters.text: ‘Then we heard Michael's trumpet calling the angels: “Thus says the Lord: Come with me to Paradise and hear the sentence concerning Adam.” God came into the garden, and the trees blossomed at his presence. His throne was set by the tree of life.’

chapters.label: Chapter 24
chapters.text: ‘God called, “Adam, where are you?” Adam answered, “I heard your voice and was afraid because I was naked.” God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree from which I commanded you not to eat?” Adam answered that the woman had given him fruit and he ate.’

chapters.label: Chapter 25
chapters.text: ‘God turned to me: “Why have you done this?” I answered, “The serpent deceived me.” Then God pronounced judgment on the serpent, on me, and on Adam. To me came pains and labour in childbirth; to Adam toil, sweat, hardship, and return to the dust.’

chapters.label: Chapter 26
chapters.text: ‘God commanded that we be driven from Paradise. We begged for a little time to eat from the tree of life, but God said that it could not be given then. He promised that if we guarded ourselves from evil, at the resurrection he would raise us and give the tree of life to the righteous.’

chapters.label: Chapter 27
chapters.text: ‘We asked at least for fragrant things from Paradise to offer worship and for seed to plant outside. God allowed the angels to give us certain spices and seeds. Then we went out of the garden, and the gate was shut behind us.’

chapters.label: Chapter 28
chapters.text: Having told this, Eve said to her children, ‘Now you know how death came upon us.’ Adam's pain grew stronger. He sent Seth with Eve toward Paradise to ask for oil from the tree of mercy, so that he might be anointed and find relief.

chapters.label: Chapter 29
chapters.text: On the way a wild beast attacked Seth. Eve cried, ‘Woe to me, for because of my sin the beasts have authority against us!’ Seth rebuked the beast: ‘Shut your mouth. How dare you attack the image of God?’ The beast answered that its hostility had arisen through human disobedience, but at Seth's command it withdrew.

chapters.label: Chapter 30
chapters.text: Eve and Seth reached the gate of Paradise and wept. Michael appeared and said, ‘Why do you ask for the oil of mercy?’ Seth answered that his father was suffering and close to death.

chapters.label: Chapter 31
chapters.text: Michael said, ‘The oil cannot be given now. It will be given in the last days, when all flesh is raised. Then the righteous will receive the delights of Paradise and God will dwell among them. Return to your father, for his time is complete. In six days his soul will leave the body.’

chapters.label: Chapter 32
chapters.text: They returned and told Adam. Eve sat beside him and said, ‘All our suffering is because of me. Let half your pain be placed upon me, because I brought the transgression upon you.’ Adam answered that his appointed time had come.

chapters.label: Chapter 33
chapters.text: Adam told Eve to gather their children after his death and tell them the whole story of their creation and fall, so that they would fear God and not repeat their parents' disobedience. Then Adam's soul departed.

chapters.label: Chapter 34
chapters.text: The sun and moon were darkened. Eve and Seth saw a chariot of light and hosts of angels. They fell to the ground in fear. Seth said, ‘What are these heavenly signs?’ Eve answered, ‘Perhaps they have come for your father.’

chapters.label: Chapter 35
chapters.text: They saw incense rising and heard angelic voices. Michael and the angels came to Adam's body. God himself was described as coming with mercy, and the heavenly powers cried, ‘Holy, holy, holy is the Lord; the glory of the Lord fills his creation.’

chapters.label: Chapter 36
chapters.text: Eve saw two great mysteries standing before God and asked Seth who they were. Seth said that they were the sun and moon, fallen down before the Lord because Adam, the image of God, had died.

chapters.label: Chapter 37
chapters.text: The angels prayed concerning Adam. One of the seraphim cried out, ‘Holy Lord, forgive Adam, for he is your image and the work of your hands.’ God had compassion on the one he had made.

chapters.label: Chapter 38
chapters.text: God said to Michael, ‘Raise Adam and bring him into Paradise, to the third heaven, until the great day that I have appointed for judgment.’ Michael carried out the command, and the angels praised God for his mercy.

chapters.label: Chapter 39
chapters.text: God commanded Michael to prepare Adam's body for burial. Michael brought linen and fragrant things from Paradise. The body of Abel was also brought, for it had not yet received its final burial. Adam and Abel were buried together in the place God appointed.

chapters.label: Chapter 40
chapters.text: God sealed Adam's grave and said, ‘Adam, Adam.’ The body answered from the earth, ‘Here I am, Lord.’ God said, ‘As I told you: earth you are and to earth you shall return. Yet I will raise you in my resurrection.’

chapters.label: Chapter 41
chapters.text: Six days after Adam's death, Eve understood that her own death was near. She gathered all her sons and daughters and said, ‘Hear me. After I die, do not mourn for me beyond six days, for the seventh day is the sign of the resurrection and the rest of the coming age.’

chapters.label: Chapter 42
chapters.text: Eve lifted her eyes toward heaven and prayed: ‘God of all, receive my spirit. Deliver me from the adversary and bring me to Adam.’ When she had finished praying, she lay down and died.

chapters.label: Chapter 43
chapters.text: Michael came and instructed Seth concerning Eve's burial. They buried her beside Adam and Abel, using the fragrances that remained. Michael warned them not to mourn more than six days and commanded them to keep the seventh day holy. Then the angel returned to heaven, praising God, and Seth and his family continued upon the earth.
